acceptedFindings.title: Missing proportional hazards assumption testing
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Cox regression requires the proportional hazards assumption to produce valid hazard ratios. Without formal testing (e.g., Schoenfeld residuals, log-log plots), the reported treatment effect may be invalid or misleading.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute Schoenfeld residuals and report a global test for each covariate and overall. Provide scaled Schoenfeld residual plots or a log-log survival plot to assess proportionality.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check diagnostics.json for presence of 'proportional_hazards_tests' or similar field with p-values.

acceptedFindings.title: Variable definitions and coding are missing
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Interpretation of hazard ratios depends entirely on variable coding: whether treatment is binary, how aging is scaled (per year, per decade), whether severity is continuous or categorical, and what event/survival_time represent. Without definitions, the numeric results are meaningless.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide explicit definitions for every variable: measurement unit, category labels, reference group if applicable, and data source. For continuous variables, state the unit of increment corresponding to the HR.

acceptedFindings.title: Insufficient adjustment for confounding
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Observational studies require a plausible confounder selection strategy (e.g., DAG, literature-based) to reduce bias. Using only age and severity likely leaves substantial residual confounding, making the association between treatment and outcome unreliable.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Develop a causal diagram, identify a minimally sufficient adjustment set, and either include those variables in a multivariable model or use propensity score methods. Provide a sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding.

acceptedFindings.title: No Cox model diagnostics provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Validity of Cox regression depends on proportional hazards assumption, absence of influential observations, and correct functional form of covariates. Without these checks, estimates may be biased or misleading.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add tests for proportional hazards (e.g., Schoenfeld residuals), multicollinearity (VIF), influential points (deviance residuals), and functional form (martingale residuals). Report test statistics and indicate whether assumptions are met.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing data handling not described
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis (n=240) can introduce selection bias if missingness is related to exposure, outcome, or covariates. Without reporting the amount and pattern of missingness, readers cannot assess potential bias.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report missingness proportions per variable, compare characteristics of excluded vs. included subjects, and consider multiple imputation or a sensitivity analysis (e.g., pattern-mixture model).

acceptedFindings.title: Lack of descriptive statistics
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a baseline characteristics table (Table 1), it is impossible to assess comparability of treatment groups, potential confounding, or generalizability of the sample.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a table summarizing demographic and clinical features by treatment arm, with appropriate statistical comparisons (standardized differences preferred over p-values).

acceptedFindings.title: Insufficient model diagnostics beyond event count
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The only diagnostic provided is number of events (140) and predictors (3). Model fit, influential observations, or assumption checks (linearity, additivity) are absent, undermining trust in the estimates.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report model fit statistics (e.g., concordance, R²), check for non-linearity (martingale residuals), and assess influential points (dfbetas).

acceptedFindings.title: Missing descriptive statistics and event counts by group
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot assess comparability of treatment groups, distribution of covariates, or number of events per group, which are essential for interpreting hazard ratios and assessing model stability.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a Table 1 with baseline characteristics (age, severity) stratified by treatment, including number of participants, events, censored cases, and median follow-up time.

acceptedFindings.title: Complete-case analysis without missing data assessment
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: If missingness is not completely at random, complete-case analysis can yield biased estimates. The extent and pattern of missingness are unknown.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the number of records excluded due to missing data, missingness per variable, and consider sensitivity analysis (e.g., multiple imputation) if missingness is non-trivial.

acceptedFindings.title: Reproducibility not assured: no analysis code or raw data
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without the analysis script or a de-identified dataset, independent verification is impossible. The artifact inventory hash covers only outputs, not the code or input data.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include the exact analysis code (e.g., R/Python notebook) that produced the results, along with session information and a synthetic or de-identified version of the dataset.

acceptedFindings.title: Data and analysis code not provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Although artifacts are listed, the raw data and the execution scripts are not available, limiting full reproducibility.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a de-identified version of the dataset and all analysis scripts in a public repository (e.g., OSF, GitHub) or state why this is not possible.

acceptedFindings.title: Treatment variable not clearly defined
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Hazard ratio interpretation requires knowing the reference category and whether treatment is binary, categorical, or continuous.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly define the treatment variable, including its levels and the contrast used in the model (e.g., treated vs. untreated).

acceptedFindings.title: Figure QA warning for zero figures
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: A warning for missing figures when no figures are expected may indicate a configuration issue and could obscure other quality problems.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Update the figure QA step to handle empty figure manifests without a warning, or confirm that no figures are needed.

finding.title: Overly defensive claims border on meta-commentary
finding.whyItMatters: Phrases like 'methods review is required before stronger claims' and 'this report is bound to the artifacts...' are unusual in a scientific manuscript and may undermine reader confidence.
finding.actionableFix: Phrase limitations in standard scientific language (e.g., 'This study is observational and cannot prove causality; results may not generalize beyond the study population.') without referencing the review process itself.

finding.title: Model convergence not reported
finding.whyItMatters: Cox models can fail to converge or produce warnings; absence of this information leaves uncertainty about numerical stability.
finding.actionableFix: Report whether the model converged and include any warnings from the fitting procedure.

finding.title: Overemphasis on precise p-values
finding.whyItMatters: Despite the ASA caution in QA, the manuscript highlights p-values prominently, which may overstate their importance.
finding.actionableFix: De‑emphasize p-values in the narrative; focus on effect sizes, confidence intervals, and clinical relevance. Mention the ASA statement.
